findings.claim: The frozen preregistration comment is now false in two places: it says "A future adapter must still identify/count with its actual tokenizer and fail closed above this ceiling before any call" and "The framing allowance is an offline contract-proof constant ... No runtime adapter consumes it", while lib/promptRefinerShadowLiveAdapter.ts:183-193 consumes PROMPT_REFINER_MESSAGE_FRAMING_TOKEN_ALLOWANCE at runtime and gates dispatch on the byte bound with no tokenizer.
findings.reproduction: Read lib/promptRefinerExecutionContract.ts:60-67, then lib/promptRefinerShadowLiveAdapter.ts:183-193 and :231-236: the allowance is added inside promptRefinerRenderedInputTokenUpperBound and the result is the only pre-dispatch ceiling check. Expected: the contract comment either states that the shadow adapter consumes it as a conservative bound, or the adapter documents the divergence.

findings.claim: The policy names the adapter `promptRefiner-openai-sdk-adapter-v1`, but the shipped constant is `prompt-refiner-openai-sdk-adapter-v1`, so the policy cites a version string that exists nowhere in code.
findings.reproduction: Grep `promptRefiner-openai-sdk-adapter-v1` -> only docs/policy/prompt-refiner-observability.md:351. Grep `prompt-refiner-openai-sdk-adapter-v1` -> lib/promptRefinerShadowRunContract.ts:23-24 (PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_ADAPTER_VERSION). Expected: the two strings match.

findings.claim: PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_CORPUS_DIGEST re-declares a third copy of the corpus digest literal already exported as PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_ADMISSION_CORPUS_DIGEST, and nothing asserts the two are equal, so the run contract does not actually bind the existing corpus identity constant required by criterion 1.
findings.reproduction: Compare lib/promptRefinerShadowRunContract.ts:25-26 with lib/promptRefinerShadowAdmissionCore.ts:94-95 (identical literal bcb2709f...). Edit only the admission-core literal (as a future corpus re-freeze would) and run `npm run test:prompt-refiner-shadow-live-adapter`: it still passes with the stale run-contract literal and the run-contract digest check does not fire. Expected: import the existing constant, or add a problem check that the two are equal.

findings.claim: The unreachable-boundary test scans only app/, lib/ and scripts/, so an import from components/ (191 files, may contain server components), .railway/ or a root entry file such as instrumentation.ts would not be caught by the guard that is this change's primary safety mechanism.
findings.reproduction: Add `import "@/lib/promptRefinerShadowLiveAdapter";` to any file under components/ or to instrumentation.ts, then run `npm run test:prompt-refiner-shadow-live-adapter`: it still passes with offenders === []. Expected: the scan covers every repository source root outside tests/ (or explicitly documents why three directories are sufficient).

findings.claim: The cost upper bound is computed when only inputTokens and outputTokens are safe integers, whereas criterion 6 states it is computed only when input/output/reasoning/cache-read counts are all safe integers; the value stays a valid upper bound under the pinned reasoningTokenBilling=billed_as_output and cachedInputPriceMultiplier=1, but the divergence is unstated.
findings.reproduction: Call the adapter with usage `{ inputTokens: 100, outputTokens: 20 }` (no inputTokenDetails/outputTokenDetails): outcome.usage.reasoningTokens and cachedInputTokens are null while costUpperBoundMicroUsd is 44. Expected: either require all four counts, or a comment stating why input+output alone still bound the cost.

verdict.nextAction: Approve as-is; the author may fold the doc/comment drift (findings 1-3) and the wider import scan (finding 4) into a follow-up revision, since no boundary, cost or reachability criterion is violated.
